claim: At grant, US4668595A lists inventors Akira Yoshino, Kenichi Sanechika, and Takayuki Nakajima and is assigned to Asahi Kasei Kogyo Kabushiki Kaisha, documenting corporate industrial R&D ownership of a nonaqueous secondary-battery architecture using layered composite oxide and/or specified n-doped carbonaceous active material.
metric_value: Asahi Kasei assignee; Yoshino / Sanechika / Nakajima inventorship
notes: Origin / ownership facts from the patent document. Not a commercial value amount and not an exact marketed-battery mapping.

claim: Mizushima, Jones, Wiseman & Goodenough (Mater. Res. Bull. 15, 783–789, 1980) report Li_xCoO2 as a new high-energy-density intercalation cathode material, establishing a pre-T0 layered-oxide cathode platform later combined with carbonaceous anodes in practical Li-ion cell designs.
notes: Pre-T0 scientific platform context supporting technical continuity of LCO-type cathodes. Not E3 product mapping and not patent-level attributable value for US4668595.

claim: US4302518A (Goodenough / Mizushima; granted 1981-11-24) discloses Li_xM_yO2 solid-solution electrodes with α-NaCrO2-type layers (including Li/Co systems) and electrochemical cells using such electrodes, establishing a pre-T0 patented cathode-chemistry platform referenced by later practical nonaqueous secondary-battery architectures.
notes: Pre-T0 patent platform continuity for layered lithium transition-metal oxide cathodes. Not a marketed Li-ion product mapping.

claim: The granted patent discloses a practical nonaqueous secondary-battery architecture combining (I) layered composite oxide A_xM_yN_zO2 active material and/or (II) n-doped carbonaceous material within specified BET / Lc / density windows, with working examples reporting reversible Li+ uptake, multi-hundred-cycle charging, and high energy density per negative-electrode active material — a public lab/prototype option signal for a future small/light rechargeable battery platform years before mass-market Li-ion commercialization.
value_carrier: aspirational nonaqueous Li-ion secondary-battery platform (not a marketed product at T0)
metric_value: carbonaceous anode + layered composite-oxide cathode secondary cell with cycle/energy-density lab examples
notes: Package B option/future-value signal observable before Sony 1991 commercial Li-ion. Must not be read as R3 implementation in a marketed consumer battery at T0=1987-05-26.

claim: The granted patent claims a secondary battery with nonaqueous electrolyte using the specified layered composite oxide and/or n-doped carbonaceous active material, framed for small, light secondary batteries with improved cyclicity, self-discharge, and energy density relative to prior lead-acid / NiCd / metallic-lithium approaches.
value_carrier: claimed nonaqueous secondary-battery platform (patent text; no marketed carrier confirmed at T0)
metric_value: nonaqueous secondary battery with layered composite oxide and/or specified carbonaceous active material
notes: Claimed/described future device uses support option-horizon interpretation. They are not proof that any marketed Li-ion battery embodied this exact patent at T0.
